thread.title: Zuckerberg appears to be done apologizing for Facebook and taking Tim Cook’s punches

author: Therese Poletti
title: Zuckerberg appears to be done apologizing for Facebook and taking Tim Cook’s punches
text:
Facebook Inc. Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg appears to be done apologizing for the massive list of issues and mishaps at the world’s largest social network, and taking punches from other tech executives without a response.
“Overall, this has been an important year,” Zuckerberg told analysts Tuesday on the company’s call to discuss its third-quarter results, which beat on earnings but slightly missed on revenue. “It’s been a tough year, but we built products that I’m proud of and we made a lot of progress on some of our hardest issues.”
Those issues were plenty, from the Cambridge Analytica scandal, two days of Congressional hearings and just last month, a data breach affecting up to 90 million users. Zuckerberg has spent a lot of time on conference calls this year apologizing and explaining those issues and describing Facebook’s responses, but on Tuesday he did not apologize once while seeming to focus on a pitch to Wall Street that the company has everything under control.
See Also What Is Gab and Who Uses It? × More from earnings season: Amazon was almost worth $1 trillion, now it’s worth less than Microsoft
During the call, the stock zigzagged up and down, but seemed to settle into gains after Chief Financial Officer David Wehner gave a forecast calling for fourth-quarter revenue growth “to decelerate by a mid- to high-single-digit percentage,” slightly better than last quarter’s “nightmare guidance.” After the call, Facebook FB, +2.91% shares were up nearly 3% in after-hours trading.
“We continue to face increased safety and security threats,” Zuckerberg said in his veiled mention of the big data breach, a controversy that likely would have received much more airtime a few months ago. “We have significantly improved our systems here, but we have more to do.”
One analyst wondered if the company’s hefty spending on building out more data centers, adding more employees and other resources to improve its security will continue ad infinitum or if there is a foreseeable end. Zuckerberg acknowledged that there is no quick fix to solve all security issues, but did give a time frame.
“There’s no silver bullet where you do the thing and then you’re done,” he said. “That said, I do think that we were quite behind where we needed to be a couple of years ago. We started a road map which we said was going to be about a three-year road map,” adding that by the end of 2019, Facebook’s AI systems should be at the level where they can flag problematic content.
Don’t miss: Facebook stock seesaws after earnings beat, but gains after forecast isn’t as scary
As Facebook has faced so many issues in the past year, it has become a punching bag for other tech executives, which Zuckerberg has mostly ignored while trying to deal with the problems at hand. On Tuesday, he seemed to punch back against Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.50% , after Chief Executive Tim Cook has repeatedly called out Facebook for privacy issues .
Zuckerberg said that Facebook Messenger and WhatsApp were leading in countries where Apple’s iPhone was not the leading device, subtly suggesting the most valuable company in the world receives an unfair advantage from bundling its iMessage instant-messaging app with its phones. Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, +1.43% GOOG, +1.58% has already faced antitrust charges for the way it bundles the Android operating system with its apps.
Zuckerberg also took a big swipe at Apple’s controversial move to store the keys to its Chinese users’ iCloud accounts in China , to comply with new Chinese laws.
“ In countries where there’s more competition between iOS and Android, like much of Europe, people tend to prefer our services,” Zuckerberg said. “Now, it’s worth noting that one of the main reasons people prefer our services, especially WhatsApp, is because of its stronger record on privacy. WhatsApp is completely end-to-end encrypted, does not store your messages and doesn’t store the keys to your messages in China or anywhere else.”
See also: Technology-stock valuations are returning to Earth
Zuckerberg’s bluster cannot overcompensate for how the issues of the past year have had an impact on the company’s revenue and user growth in some markets. Revenue of $13.7 billion in the third quarter grew at 33%, slowing down from 42% revenue growth in the second quarter and 49% in the first quarter. Daily users in the U.S. and Canada, its fourth-largest geographic section for users but most important in terms of revenue, remained flat in the third quarter after very little growth in the first two quarters of this year. And the company is looking for continued revenue deceleration in the fourth quarter.
Zuckerberg is clearly done with apologies and focusing on the negative with Facebook. If he wants to win back investors he lost, though, he needs to fix what’s ailing the company financially while continuing to fight the problems that have put him in a compromised position in the first place.
